AWPTCM-T33242.objective:
• An ICMP Echo Reply uses the same source IP address as the specific-destination address of the corresponding Echo Request.
  • The device responds to ICMP Echo Requests sent to its configured IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
  • The TTL in ICMP responses is not taken from the packet that triggered the response.
  • ICMP Echo Replies are correctly generated from all members of a VCS/stack.
  • ICMP traffic is correctly permitted or denied by hardware and QoS ACLs.
  • The device responds to ICMP Route Redirect messages and updates its routing table accordingly.
  • A DHCP server correctly uses ICMP to probe for IP address conflicts.
  • The device generates ICMP Destination Unreachable messages when appropriate.
  • The device generates ICMP Time Exceeded messages when a packet's TTL expires.
  • The device generates ICMP Parameter Problem messages for malformed packets.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Send an ICMP Echo Request to a configured address. Verify the Echo Reply uses the same source IP as the destination of the original request.
Send ICMP Echo Requests to both IPv4 and IPv6 configured addresses. Confirm the device responds correctly.
Verify that the TTL in ICMP responses is set independently and not copied from the triggering packet.
In a VCS/stack, send ICMP Echo Requests to member addresses. Confirm correct Echo Replies are generated from the appropriate members.
Send ICMP Route Redirect messages to the device. Confirm it updates its routing table accordingly.
Trigger conditions that should generate Destination Unreachable, Time Exceeded, and Parameter Problem messages. Verify correct generation.
